rounds.proof_sketch: K=4096 is exactly divisible by BLOCK_SIZE=16. Tile loop runs t=0..255. Maximum A_col = 255*16+15 = 4095 < K=4096. The mutated condition A_col<=K vs A_col<K differs only when A_col==K, which never occurs in this configuration.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes the A tile load condition from A_col < K to A_col <= K. With K=4096 and BLOCK_SIZE=16, K is perfectly divisible by the block size. The tile loop iterates exactly 256 times (t=0 to 255), and A_col = t*16 + threadCol ranges from 0 to 4095. Since A_col never equals 4096, both conditions (A_col < 4096 and A_col <= 4096) evaluate identically for all reachable A_col values. The boundary case where A_col == K would require K to NOT be a multiple of BLOCK_SIZE, which would make the final tile's A_col potentially equal K for some threads.
rounds.kill_strategy: This mutant requires K to not be a multiple of BLOCK_SIZE (e.g., K=4097) to be killed. With the fixed shape K=4096 being perfectly divisible by 16, the predicate difference is unreachable. No value-level test can distinguish the mutation under the given shape constraints.
rounds.recommendations: When designing mutation testing for tiled GPU kernels, include test shapes where dimensions are NOT multiples of the tile/block size (e.g., K=4097, K=4080+1) to properly exercise boundary condition handling. Align-friendly dimensions like 4096 can mask off-by-one errors in boundary checks.
